reason: Both answers get the core numbers right (LTV $3,200, 4:1 LTV:CAC, 8.3-month payback, ~31% annual churn) and reach a similar verdict. A is better calibrated and quantifies the churn fix (3% to 2% gives LTV $4,800, 6:1). It also adds the fully-loaded CAC check and the point that cohort churn may flatten. B adds a useful cash-timing argument for annual prepay. It also overstates that most VCs would pass without expansion, and it gives an unsupported $5–10M ARR ceiling. A's verdict is closer to the expected "fundable, churn is the thing to fix."
